results.name: player_control_update_local_player_action
results.evidence: Indexes the per-local-player struct at DAT_006b145c+0x10+idx*0x40 (same struct used by chimera__spectate_fp_camera_position and the weapon-index helpers below), calls the look-angle updater FUN_00472160 and weapon/grenade cycling helpers (FUN_0056bee0/FUN_0056bdc0/FUN_0056bfc0), and for local players appends the built action into the DAT_006f7ea4 client-update queue (matches update_client_new's queue).
results.summary: Per-tick processing of one local player's action state: reads the current action/control flags, cycles the selected weapon and grenade type, forwards look-angle updates, and queues the resulting action for network transmission.

results.name: player_recompute_look_vector
results.evidence: Both branches of the (effectively dead) conditional on in_CX unconditionally call FUN_00473d70, which builds a forward/look vector from pitch and yaw.
results.summary: Thin wrapper around the look-vector computation FUN_00473d70 for a given local-player/unit context.

results.name: unit_get_camera_pitch_limit
results.evidence: Default return value 1.2217305 rad (~70 degrees) matches Halo's look-pitch clamp; when the unit's active weapon (via the 0x2f2 index into the 0xbe weapon-object array) is a zoom weapon, the limit is instead computed from a per-object-type field at offset 0x1a0 through FUN_004c2e50.
results.summary: Returns the maximum look-pitch angle for a unit, using a zoom-weapon-specific value when the unit is holding a scoped weapon, otherwise a fixed default.

results.name: unit_get_first_person_camera_position
results.evidence: Earlier RE hint named this chimera__spectate_fp_camera_position; code fills a 3-field output with an object index/salt and a position derived from a weapon's camera marker (object_try_and_get(2), marker table offset 0x2e8 + weapon-marker-index*0x11c) or, absent a weapon marker, from the unit's own default camera marker at offset 0x1a8.
results.summary: Computes the first-person camera object/offset for a local player's controlled unit, preferring the currently held weapon's camera marker over the unit's own.

results.name: unit_set_local_player_weapon_index
results.evidence: Looks up the unit's owning-player back-reference at offset 0x218, resolves that player's local-player slot, and writes param_1 into the local-player struct at (slot*0x40+0x30+DAT_006b145c) — the same field read by FUN_00472740/FUN_004726b0 as the tracked weapon index.
results.summary: Updates the HUD-tracked current weapon index for whichever local player owns the given unit.

results.name: player_update_look_angles
results.evidence: Operates on the same per-local-player struct (idx*0x40+0x10+DAT_006b145c) as FUN_00471ae0, adjusts a stored yaw value using chimera__spectate_fp_camera_position and vector3d_angle_between_4cd4f0 for vehicle/turret facing limits, then clamps and integrates pitch/yaw with per-tick step limits (0.012271847 rad).
results.summary: Updates a local player's look yaw/pitch each tick, clamping against any vehicle seat facing constraints and limiting the per-tick turn rate.

results.name: unit_get_local_player_weapon_index
results.evidence: Resolves the unit's owning player via the 0x218 back-reference then reads the local-player struct field at offset 0x30 (weapon index) combined with the salt at 0x32, mirroring the setter FUN_00472100.
results.summary: Returns the full weapon datum index (index+salt) tracked for the local player controlling this unit, or -1 if none.

results.name: unit_invalidate_local_player_weapon_index
results.evidence: Same owning-player lookup as FUN_004726b0 but writes 0xffff into the local-player struct field at offset 0x34 (the weapon salt paired with the 0x30 index field), forcing a refresh.
results.summary: Invalidates the cached weapon-index salt for the local player controlling the given unit.

results.name: local_player_get_weapon_index
results.evidence: Directly indexes the per-local-player struct by in_CX (no unit lookup step) and returns the same 0x30/0x34 weapon-index/salt pair read by FUN_004726b0.
results.summary: Returns the tracked current weapon datum index for a given local player slot.

results.name: player_control_digitize_action_flags
results.evidence: Builds bit flags (0x1,0x2,0x4,0x8,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x80/0x100,0x200/0x400,0x800/0x1000,0x2000/0x4000) into *DAT_006b145c from an input struct (in_EDX) based on button/analog-sign tests; the exact same bit values (0x18,0x20,0x1,0x2,0x4) are consumed later in FUN_00471ae0's local_24 flags.
results.summary: Converts a raw unit-control input structure into digitized action-flag bits accumulated in the global local-player control header.

results.name: update_server_new
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint confirmed by code: zeroes the server-queue globals block, allocates it via data_new("update server queues",0x10), and on success zeroes the remainder and calls update_client_new.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes the server-side network update-queue globals, then initializes the paired client-side queue.

results.name: update_queues_dispose
results.evidence: Frees both DAT_006f1d90 (server queue, allocated by update_server_new) and DAT_006f7ed0 (client queue, allocated by update_client_new) via GlobalFree and resets their tracking globals.
results.summary: Frees and resets both the server-side and client-side network update-queue allocations.

results.name: update_server_dispose
results.evidence: Marks DAT_006f1d90+0x24, calls data_delete_all twice on the server queue's datum array, iterates remaining entries invoking FUN_00479f40 per entry, then calls the client-side counterpart FUN_00472fa0.
results.summary: Tears down the server update queue's datum array and cascades into disposing the client update queue.

results.name: update_server_queue_new_entry
results.evidence: Calls datum_new_at_index_with_salt (creating/reusing a queue slot at a fixed index+salt) followed by the per-entry init helper FUN_00479f40 also used in FUN_00472b70's cleanup loop.
results.summary: Creates (or reinitializes) a single entry in the server update-queue datum array.

results.name: update_server_queue_push_tick
results.evidence: Advances a 32-slot ring-buffer cursor (DAT_006f1d8c masked with 0x1f, slot stride 0xc2 dwords) and, for each player datum returned by data_iterator_next, copies fields between a per-player circular buffer (offsets 0x28-0x40 of the player record) and the new ring slot.
results.summary: Pushes a new server-tick history entry for every player into a 32-deep per-player ring buffer used for network delta reconciliation.

results.name: update_server_queue_read_entry
results.evidence: Given a tick index in in_ECX, bounds-checks it against DAT_006f1d8c and copies a 0xc1-dword slot out of the DAT_006f1d98 ring buffer (same stride 0xc2 used by FUN_00472cc0) into the caller's output buffer.
results.summary: Looks up and copies a previously pushed server-queue history entry for a requested tick index.

results.name: update_client_new
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint confirmed by code: zeroes the client-queue globals block and allocates it via data_new("update client queues",0x10), initializing the ring-buffer indices on success.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes the client-side network update-queue globals and its ring-buffer state.

results.name: update_client_dispose
results.evidence: Mirrors FUN_00472b70 but operates on DAT_006f7ed0 (the client queue allocated by update_client_new): marks it for teardown and drains it via data_delete_all/data_iterator_next.
results.summary: Tears down the client update queue's datum array.

results.name: update_client_queue_build_entry
results.evidence: Copies 8 dwords from in_EAX plus two extra fields (DAT_006f7eac/DAT_006f7ea8) into a local scratch buffer, then writes the merged result into DAT_006f7ea4, the same staging struct consumed by FUN_00473270 and FUN_00471ae0.
results.summary: Builds a staged client update entry from raw input data plus extra state, ready to be queued for sending to the server.

results.name: update_server_apply_client_queue_tick
results.evidence: Calls FUN_00473500 (the client-queue slot accessor) to fetch a tick's queued entry, then iterates player data copying an 0x20-byte struct and a separate 0x10-byte sub-struct out of the queue slot into two output buffers, incrementing DAT_006f7e9c.
results.summary: Applies a queued client update for a given tick to the server's per-player runtime state.

results.name: update_client_queue_apply_entry_to_players
results.evidence: Copies the current staged entry at DAT_006f7ea4 (built by FUN_00473090) into an output array once per item returned by data_iterator_next, incrementing DAT_006f7e9c.
results.summary: Distributes the currently staged client update entry into a per-player output array and advances the update tick counter.

results.name: update_server_run_ticks
results.evidence: When unaff_BX (a tick count) is positive, advances a wraparound history cursor (DAT_007102d4 masked to 6 bits), pushes the current staged entry via FUN_00473390, then repeatedly calls the ring-buffer push/read pair FUN_00472cc0/FUN_00472ea0.
results.summary: Runs the server update-queue push/read cycle for a given number of catch-up ticks.

results.name: update_server_queue_push_player_entry
results.evidence: Maps a player index through DAT_006b1460 to a per-player ring buffer (stride 100 within the DAT_006f1d90 queue block, read/write cursors at offsets 0x28/0x2c/0x30/0x34) and inserts the 8-dword param_1 entry if the buffer has free space.
results.summary: Pushes an update entry into a specific player's server-side history ring buffer if space is available.

results.name: server_find_player_by_name
results.evidence: Only runs when DAT_00719720==2 (server); fetches a name into local_800 via FUN_00557990 and compares it against each player's name field via _wcscmp while walking data_iterator_next. callers=0, so this may be dead or reached only indirectly.
results.summary: Server-side helper that scans all players comparing names, likely for a console/RCON player-lookup command.

results.name: update_client_queue_advance_read_cursor
results.evidence: Uses FUN_00473500 to fetch/advance queue slots, comparing against a target tick (unaff_EBX) and DAT_006f7ea0, invalidating skipped slots' salt field (offset 4) to -1 as it advances.
results.summary: Advances the client update-queue read cursor toward a target tick, discarding any stale intervening entries.

results.name: update_client_queue_get_slot
results.evidence: Branches on DAT_00719720: as a client (mode 1) it returns the next write slot in the DAT_006f7ed4 128-entry ring buffer via a round-robin index (DAT_006887b0); as server/single-player it returns a slot only if the requested tick index falls within the current DAT_006f7e9c..+0x80 window.
results.summary: Returns a pointer to a slot in the 128-entry client update ring buffer, either allocating the next write slot (client) or looking up a slot by tick (server/single-player).

results.name: random_get_table_point
results.evidence: Uses the classic Blam LCG constants (0x19660d / 0x3c6ef35f) to advance DAT_00719cd0, then indexes a vector3d lookup table (DAT_006b7af4, count DAT_006b7af8) and copies the 3 floats to the output pointer.
results.summary: Advances the global PRNG and returns a random point from a precomputed vector3d table, used elsewhere for respawn placement jitter.

results.name: players_initialize
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint confirmed by code: creates the "players" and "teams" datum arrays (FUN_005380d0), allocates and CRC-hashes the players_globals (0x98 bytes) and local-player control globals (0x50 bytes) blocks, storing their addresses into DAT_0087a478 and DAT_006b145c.
results.summary: Allocates and CRC-registers the players and teams datum arrays and their associated globals blocks.

results.name: players_dispose
results.evidence: Zeroes and re-initializes the players_globals struct (DAT_0087a478), calls data_delete_all on both the players (DAT_0087a480) and teams (DAT_0087a47c) datum arrays, and resets the local-player-to-player map (DAT_006b1460, 16 entries) to -1.
results.summary: Resets the players and teams datum arrays and clears the local-player mapping table.

results.name: players_team_has_member
results.evidence: Iterates the players datum array via data_iterator_next comparing each player's team field (offset 2) against an implicit parameter (unaff_ESI).
results.summary: Checks whether any player belongs to a given team.

results.name: teams_find_available_team_index
results.evidence: Walks a fixed 4-entry team-slot table (DAT_006b2ce8, -1 sentinel) calling FUN_004736d0 (players_team_has_member) to find a slot that is either unused or has no members.
results.summary: Finds an available (empty or unassigned) team slot for assigning a new player.

results.name: player_new_basic
results.evidence: Allocates a player datum (datum_new / datum_new_at_index) on the DAT_0087a480 players array, sets its name via _wcsncpy and a smaller set of default fields (up to offset ~0x188) than the larger FUN_00473940, then registers it into DAT_006b1460.
results.summary: Creates a new player datum with a reduced field-initialization set and links it into the local-player map.

results.name: player_new
results.evidence: Allocates a player datum (datum_new / datum_new_at_index_with_salt) on DAT_0087a480, sets name and team, and when param_2 (team) is -1 performs additional full initialization (FUN_00479f40, FUN_0047a020, FUN_0047a250, more field resets up to offset 0x1f8) before registering the index into DAT_006b1460.
results.summary: Creates a new player datum, performing full state initialization for a freshly-created (as opposed to network-replicated) player.

results.name: player_delete
results.evidence: Calls FUN_0045c570 (unrelated cleanup), frees a per-player allocation at offset 0x134 when acting as client (DAT_00719720==1) or calls FUN_004e0b90 when server, removes the player from DAT_006b1460, then calls datum_delete.
results.summary: Frees a player's dynamic allocations, unlinks it from the local-player map, and deletes its datum.

results.name: player_remove
results.evidence: Frees a server-only per-player 100-byte ring buffer allocation (offset 0x3c, matching the stride used in FUN_00473390), calls player_delete (FUN_00473ae0) and FUN_004e9d40, then clears a byte in the DAT_006b0b88 roster array using an index from FUN_00466e80.
results.summary: Full removal of a player: frees network history buffers, deletes the player datum, and clears its roster slot.

results.name: unit_apply_camera_recoil
results.evidence: Looks up a per-weapon-type recoil definition (DAT_00746f8c+0x34c indexed by in_AX*0x68) and accumulates its offset fields into the unit's camera-offset fields (offset 0xe0/0xe4/0x31e), optionally resetting them first when param_1 is set.
results.summary: Accumulates or resets a weapon's recoil/kick offset into a unit's camera state.

results.name: unit_compute_facing_and_gravity_vector
results.evidence: Computes a forward vector via cos/sin of pitch and yaw (in_ECX[0],[1]) into the output vector, then for units without the appropriate object flag transforms a normalized velocity vector through the object's parent matrix (matrix4x3_transform_normal) via object_try_and_get(2).
results.summary: Computes a unit's forward-facing vector from its view angles and additionally adjusts a velocity/gravity-related vector relative to its parent object.

results.name: players_ensure_units_after_bsp_switch
results.evidence: Attempts to find a valid placement (object_iterator_next / FUN_0056c070 / FUN_0042c3e0) then iterates players looking for those with unit_index==-1, attempting to spawn (FUN_00477ea0) and reattach them via FUN_00475c60 to the newly found parent object.
results.summary: After a structure-BSP switch, attempts to give every player without a unit a valid unit and attach it to the new BSP's parent object, retrying as needed.

results.name: game_engine_players_update
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004730d0 (server-side dequeue of queued client updates) unconditionally, then for each player checks game_engine_player_ready_to_respawn, calls FUN_004611b0 and FUN_00477ea0 to spawn, game_engine_apply_player_grenade_counts, and handles per-player weapon/zoom/melee flag bits before calling FUN_00473d70.
results.summary: Main per-tick players update used on the server/single-player path: applies queued client input, handles respawning, and processes each player's action flags.

results.name: game_engine_players_update_client
results.evidence: Structurally parallel to FUN_004740a0 (same respawn/grenade/action handling calls) but begins with FUN_00473270 (the client-side staged-update broadcaster) instead of FUN_004730d0, matching the client-only update path.
results.summary: Client-side counterpart of game_engine_players_update: applies the locally staged update and processes respawn/action handling without dequeuing the server queue.

results.name: main_switch_structure_bsp
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint confirmed by code: uses the exact referenced strings "tried to switch to current/invalid structure-bsp %d" when validating a requested BSP switch index against DAT_00746f8c+0x39c/0x3a0 before calling FUN_004aa2a0.
results.summary: Per-tick handling of structure-BSP switch triggers: validates the requested BSP index and either logs an error or performs the switch.

results.name: local_player_to_player_index
results.evidence: Returns *(DAT_0087a478+4+idx*4) — the players_globals local-player-to-player-index map also read directly in FUN_00471ae0.
results.summary: Looks up the player index currently assigned to a given local-player slot.

results.name: game_set_local_player
results.evidence: Updates the local_players[] map at DAT_0087a478+4 for slot unaff_SI, clearing the previous player's back-reference (offset 2 of its player record) and setting the new player's back-reference to the local-player slot index.
results.summary: Assigns (or clears) which player index is bound to a given local-player slot, keeping the player's back-reference in sync.

results.name: players_iterate_all
results.evidence: Walks the full players datum array via data_iterator_next with no visible per-item logic and always returns 0xffffffff; called from 18 sites, so the decompiled body likely lost side effects from the real per-item test.
results.summary: Iterates all players; the visible decompiled behavior always returns -1, so its true per-call purpose (given 18 call sites) is not fully recoverable from this view.

results.name: player_reset_after_unit_change
results.evidence: Clears the player's queued-update fields (offsets 0x34/0x38), resets the associated local-player control struct at DAT_006b145c when the player has one (offset 2 index), and recomputes the players_globals "all spawned" flag (offset 0x10) by scanning for any player still missing a unit.
results.summary: Resets a player's per-tick state and local-player control struct after its controlled unit changes, and updates the global all-players-spawned flag.

results.name: local_player_set_controlled_unit
results.evidence: Clears the previous unit's back-reference (offset 0x218) via FUN_00569bf0, sets the new unit's back-reference to the local player's player index, and stores the new unit index into the player record's unit_index field (offset 0x34).
results.summary: Binds a new unit as the controlled object for a local player, updating both the unit's owner back-reference and the player's unit-index field.

results.name: game_engine_players_any_pending_respawn
results.evidence: Iterates players checking weapon/vehicle-seat related flags (a byte at offset 0x17c bit 0x40, and a counter at offset 0x134) via FUN_0055e8e0, returning 1 as soon as a qualifying player is found.
results.summary: Scans all players and returns whether any is in a pending state requiring respawn/seat handling.

results.name: players_any_without_unit
results.evidence: Iterates players via data_iterator_next and returns 1 as soon as one is found with unit_index (offset 0x34) equal to -1, else 0.
results.summary: Returns whether any player currently lacks a controlled unit.

results.name: object_attach_player_unit_to_parent
results.evidence: callers=0 (unused/dead); structurally near-identical to FUN_00475c60 (same reparenting sequence: matrix4x3_multiply, object_for_each_light_attachment, object_recalculate_bounding_radius_recursive) but sources its offset via FUN_004f6080 instead of a caller-supplied pointer.
results.summary: Unused variant that reattaches a player's unit to a new parent object, recomputing its transform and light attachments.

results.name: object_find_valid_placement_near
results.evidence: Iterates up to 9 candidate offsets (and, on failure, 8 further randomized jitter points using the same PRNG constants as FUN_00473560) testing each via FUN_0055a500 (object placement validity test with flag 0x40000000) until a non-colliding position is found.
results.summary: Searches nearby candidate positions, including randomized jitter, for a placement where a player's unit does not collide with the world, used when attaching/respawning a unit.

results.name: player_unit_attach_to_object
results.evidence: Given a player index, resolves its unit, calls object_find_valid_placement_near (FUN_004757b0) then reparents the unit via matrix4x3_multiply/object_for_each_light_attachment/object_recalculate_bounding_radius_recursive, storing the new parent index at unit offset 0xcb.
results.summary: Attaches a player's unit as a child of a target parent object at a given local offset, updating its transform, light attachments, and bounding radius.

results.name: player_unit_update_parent_light_attachments
results.evidence: Given a player's unit-index reference, toggles light-attachment sync bits (puVar3[4] bit 1) on both the unit's current and previous parent objects via object_for_each_light_attachment, and clears the unit's local player struct via FUN_00474e10.
results.summary: Synchronizes light-attachment state on a player unit's current and former parent objects after a parenting change and resets the player's local-player struct.

results.name: player_handle_unit_death
results.evidence: Clears the unit's offset-0xe0 field, optionally records a reason code at the player's offset 0x2c, calls FUN_004eda20/FUN_00568120 (unidentified) and FUN_00474e10 (player_reset_after_unit_change).
results.summary: Handles the loss of a player's controlled unit, clearing related state and triggering the post-unit-change reset.

results.name: game_engine_server_update_player_positions
results.evidence: Server-only (DAT_00719720==2); for each player whose unit has a dirty-position flag (offset 0x4b8) it copies position/velocity fields (0xf4/0xf8/0xfc/0x100) and, for local players, logs via FUN_004e7f90 with the format string "[%d]: [%d]:\t Completed [%d] (...)" also used verbatim in the following function.
results.summary: Server-side per-tick routine that copies a moved unit's position/velocity into its owning player's record and logs completion for local players.

results.name: game_engine_server_update_player_positions_tail
results.evidence: callers=0; body is essentially a duplicate of the logging/copy loop inside FUN_00476760 (same format string "[%d]: [%d]:\t Completed [%d] (...)" and same field offsets 0x4b8/0xf4/0xf8/0xfc/0x100), with no equipment/grenade-count logic despite the inherited name from a prior session, so it is renamed to match the observed behavior.
results.summary: Appears to be a duplicated tail fragment of game_engine_server_update_player_positions (same logging and field-copy logic), not related to equipment or grenade counts as its previous name implied.

results.name: player_apply_initial_position_update
results.evidence: Only runs for a client-mode local player whose unit just became valid; checks FUN_00477210 (attachment/vehicle test) to decide between apply_remote_player_position_update and the snap variant FUN_00477490.
results.summary: Applies the first position update for a newly spawned local player's unit, choosing a smooth or snap update based on whether the unit is attached to another object.

results.name: players_client_catchup_on_server_updates
results.evidence: Referenced string "[%d]: Caught up on [%d] updates == [%d] ticks.\n" matches the function's purpose exactly; walks each player's per-tick history ring buffer (offsets 0x120/0x128/0x130/0x300) dequeuing entries until caught up to the server, applying apply_remote_player_position_update or FUN_00477490 as needed.
results.summary: Client-side routine that drains a player's buffered server updates, fast-forwarding position/orientation state until it matches the latest server tick.

results.name: unit_is_attached_to_vehicle
results.evidence: Validates a player index range against DAT_0087a480, resolves the associated unit via object_try_and_get(3), and returns true only when the unit's parent-object field (offset 0x11c) is valid, delegating the final check to FUN_0056cd10.
results.summary: Tests whether a given player's unit currently has a valid parent object (e.g. is boarding or seated in a vehicle).

results.name: players_find_local_player_owned
results.evidence: Iterates players checking the local-player back-reference field (offset 2) for a non-(-1) value, but the decompiled code returns 0xffffffff on every path, suggesting lost side effects similar to FUN_00474db0.
results.summary: Scans players for one owned by a local player; the decompiled return value is always -1, so its effective behavior here is unclear.

results.name: unit_snap_position_if_far
results.evidence: Computes the distance between a new position (in_EAX) and the unit's last stored position (in_ECX+0x5c/0x60/0x64); if it exceeds 1.1 units, overwrites the stored position (offset 0x68/0x6c/0x70) and sets a moved/dirty flag bit (0x20) in the unit's flag word (offset 0x10).
results.summary: Detects when a unit has moved farther than a small threshold and, if so, snaps its cached position and marks it dirty for network reconciliation.
